title: docs(react): the InlineEditContextValue.draft comment teaches the own-key read (objectui#10466)
body:
Fixes #10466
Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

The `draft` member's doc comment on the published `InlineEditContextValue` (`packages/react/src/context/InlineEditContext.tsx`) ended: "Read a field's live value as `draft[name] ?? data[name]`."

That read falls back to the saved value whenever the draft value is `null` or `undefined`. A field the user emptied is an own draft key with an empty value. So is a single select or radio emptied by a cascade clear, which stages `null` since PR objectui#10464. A host that copied the comment showed the value the user had just removed. On the highlights strip, that read handed an option widget the pruned value again on every render, an endless loop (objectui#7190; relayed from the card, not re-run here). The comment ships in the `dist` typings, so it is what a host author sees on hover.

## Measured first, on `origin/main` `6881e9e47`

I looked for every reader of the inline-edit `draft`: each `useInlineEdit()` consumer outside tests, by `git grep` over `packages/*/src` and `apps/`.

| Host | What it reads | Rule for an emptied field |
|---|---|---|
| `DetailView` (`@object-ui/plugin-detail`) | hands each section `data={{ ...data, ...editedValues }}`, where `editedValues` is the draft | spread: an own key wins |
| `DetailSection` | its `data` prop (the merged record above); from the session it reads only `fieldErrors` | inherits the spread |
| `HeaderHighlight` | `stagedRecord = { ...data, ...draft }`, then `stagedRecord[field.name]` | spread: an own key wins |
| `InlineEditSaveBar` | writes the draft; reads no live value | not a reader |
| `containers.tsx` (`@object-ui/components`) | `.editing` only | not a reader |

- The two readers agree: both use the spread.
- None of them uses an own-key test (`in draft`, `hasOwnProperty`, `Object.hasOwn`), and no exported helper does the merge. So the comment names the spread and points at no helper.
- The form hosts do not read this draft. `ObjectForm` and the form renderer keep their own form state, and the grep above finds no `useInlineEdit()` call in them.

## The change

- **Only the JSDoc sentence changes.** It now says to read the value from the staged record `{ ...data, ...draft }`. An own draft key wins even when its value is empty (`null`, `undefined`, `''`), and `data[name]` is read only when the key is absent. It does not name `??`. No runtime code changes and nothing new is exported.
- **One pin:** `packages/react/src/context/__tests__/InlineEditContext.draftReadRule-10466.test.ts`.
- **One patch changeset** for `@object-ui/react`. `check-changeset-presence` counts both touched `src/` files as published source of a released package.

## Why a pin

This package already pins prescriptive doc text by reading the source: `LazyPluginLoader.jsdocExample.test.ts` and `useNavigationOverlay.docExampleRecordSource-7638.test.ts`. The new pin follows that pattern and stays loose. It reads only the code spans of the `draft` doc comment, never its prose, and asserts two things:

1. No span reads the draft and then falls back through a nullish or falsy operator.
2. At least one span names a read that keeps an own draft key: the staged-record spread with the draft last, or an own-key test.

Each matcher has synthetic controls. They show it fires on the old spelling and on the reversed spread, and stays silent on the own-key spellings.

## Ablation: put the old doc back, watch the pin go red, restore

- **Tool:** `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode at `a0bef54ea`, inside a restore trap.
- **Mutation:** the new doc lines were replaced with the old sentence. I checked before the run that this rebuilds the BASE file byte for byte.
- **Proof it landed on disk:** the anchor count went from 1 to 0 and the replacement count from 0 to 1. The blob changed from `8457b8281762` to `0239d8089256`. By grep, spread spans went from 1 to 0 and fallback spans from 0 to 1.
- **Result:** I predicted red, and it went red: `Tests  2 failed | 3 passed (5)`. The two failures were the two assertions on the real comment; the three controls stayed green.
- **Restore:** the blob after restore equals the blob at HEAD (`8457b8281762`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty (0 bytes).
- **No build step in between:** the pin reads the `.tsx` source by path, not `dist`.

## Local verification (all at `a0bef54ea`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/react/` gave `Test Files  96 passed (96)` and `Tests  1303 passed (1303)`. The pin is in that population: `vitest list --filesOnly packages/react/` lists 96 files, and the pin is one of them.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` built types, core, data-objectstack and i18n: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check` echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The test project's `--listFiles` includes the pin (1 of its 96 test files).
- **Gates, all exit 0:**
  - `check:control-bytes`;
  - `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`);
  - `check-changeset-presence`;
  - `check:changeset-claims`: nothing flagged. The born-false reading found 0 line addresses, the self-contradiction reading was clean, and no pending changeset names a touched file;
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`;
  - `check:test-path-roots`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:shell-escape-residue`.
- **eslint, narrowed to the touched files, with the narrowing measured:**
  - Scope, from eslint itself: of the 3 touched paths, eslint ignores the changeset `.md` ("File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied").
  - Count, from `--format json`: 2 files, 0 errors, 5 warnings. The same file at BASE gives the same 5 warnings (`no-explicit-any` x4, `react-refresh/only-export-components` x1), so none of them is new.
  - Untouched files are safe: `eslint.config.js` does not enable type-aware linting (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions`, no `TypeChecked` preset; typescript-eslint appears 9 times as a control). So this diff cannot change a lint result in any untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- The published CHANGELOGs of `@object-ui/plugin-detail` and `@object-ui/app-shell` still quote the old read in their objectui#2407 P2 entries. They are historical record, so they are left alone.
- The comment in `HeaderHighlight` ("An OWN draft key wins even when its value is `undefined`") already agrees with the new doc, so it is unchanged.
